FIXTURE ARITHMETIC · THREE CORRECTIONS, STATED NOT SMUGGLED

The wireframes' cap numbers cannot all be true at once

1 · The cap gauge read 1.240 / 1.760 km on day 6 of a 31-day cycle

1.240 km over six days is 207 km/day, which projects to ≈6.400 km by 22 August — not the ≈1.410 the card claims, and nowhere near "under the cap". It also contradicts Home's own July pulse of 412 km, since 23–28 July is a subset of July. Corrected to 268 km, which is 44,7 km/day and projects to ≈1.385.

2 · "Insurance in 16 days" and "16 August 2026" are different dates

From 28 July, sixteen days is 13 August. Since the reminder hero names 16 August explicitly, the chip and every meta line are corrected to "in 19 days", and the policy's valid-until is set to 16 Aug 2026 so the Garage chip, Home's reminder and the vault card cannot disagree.

3 · The Care group has one insurance door, not two

§6.2's frame draws Insurance and Documents as separate rows; §10 then rules that two rows to one page is a nav smell and gives the meta line the second row's job. §10 is the later decision, so the drawn Care group carries one row.

§6.1 · GARAGE · DARK

Archived cars are rows, not dimmed cards

Dimming a photo card reads as broken. A row reads as shelved. Archive shelves, delete purges, and the two are never conflated — the archived car keeps its whole story one tap behind "Show archived records" in History.

The photo is identity, never data

A photoless car gets a warm placeholder block, not a grey box. And the card's accent must stop being the fuel hue — the build paints a car row green today, which both breaks the identity-only rule and spends the app's one green on something that is not fuel money.

Ordering: most-recently-active first

§16 #12's recommendation, taken. An alphabetical garage buries the car you actually drive. Archived always last. Logged as a taste call, not a derivation.

A single-car garage is still a list of one

Not a promoted dashboard. And with one car, every scope chip and car picker in the product does not render at all — that is article 8, and it is a rendering rule, not a disabled state.

Chips are facts — and one denominator, decided

The cap chip and the car page's gauge both read 268/1.760 km — the pooled budget. §5.3 allowed the chip to show the bare 1.500 instead, and drawing it that way surfaced a real contradiction.

At 1.600 km the two would disagree outright: a bare-cap chip says "100 km over" while the gauge says under budget — the disagreement §C4 forbids. My first fix synced the chip's over/under state while leaving its numbers bare, which manages the contradiction and still shows 1.600/1.500 while calling it fine. Decided instead: one denominator. The bare cap survives only where it is defined — the gauge's own line, 1.500 cap + 260 carried over from June. Simpler, and it removes the bug class rather than policing it.

02 · The car page — both ownership shapes

The PLAN group and the OWNERSHIP group never both appear. Drawing only the subscription car would have hidden half the rule.

§6.2 · CAR PAGE · OWNED OUTRIGHT · NO PLAN GROUP

Exactly three recent rows, then the link

Not five, not "a few", not scrollable. This is article 1 with a number on it, and it is the structural fix for a real defect Tester R found — duplicated history inside car sheet — whose 2.0 fix was the one-ledger rule.

The build has reintroduced it. car/[id].tsx renders every reading with an inline add form. A shipped-and-fixed defect is back, and that is the single strongest argument for this pass existing.

What is deliberately not on this page

A readings list. An inline add-reading form. A delete-car button in the body. The first two are a second copy of the ledger; the third belongs in the car form's foot with Archive and Restore, because destructive lifecycle actions belong together and behind an edit intent.

The odometer has one surface and two doors

The card's …› opens the same sheet Capture → Odometer opens, prefilled with this car. A second implementation of the same task is how two surfaces drift apart. The value itself is derived from the trail, never stored.

…› versus › is load-bearing

A bare chevron pushes a page; the ellipsis form opens a sheet. Three rows on the subscription page use each. Without the distinction a row that opens a task is indistinguishable from one that goes somewhere — and the user cannot predict whether Back or Cancel is coming.

Full history is a cross-tab jump, deliberately

It switches to the History tab with the car scope chip already set, and the arrival is visible — the chip reads Golf GTI ▾. There is one ledger and it lives on its own tab.

Two rows carry attention, quietly

The Reminders meta says ITV is 12 days over in attention, and the Insurance meta names its renewal date. Neither is a badge, neither is red. The car page and the Garage card tell the same truth in the same colour.

03 · Over-cap, the swap sheet, the payoff nudge

Three conditional blocks, each drawn on the car it can actually happen to.
OVER-CAP · GOLF GTI · 19 AUGUST, DAY 28 OF THE CYCLE
Mapfre 80 km over
1.840 / 1.760 km 23 JUL – 22 AUG
1.500 cap + 260 carried over from June.
80 km over your pooled budget.
At your pace, ≈2.035 km by 22 August.
Over-cap is never hidden: the gauge fills in attention, the overage is counted in text, and the pace line stays present tense. Nothing flashes, nothing turns red, and the chip names the pooled overage so the two surfaces agree.
Arithmetic: 1.840 km over 28 days is 65,7 km/day, which over the cycle's 31 days is ≈2.035 — so the snapshot is dated 19 August, not 28 July. A pace sentence that does not divide by the days it has is exactly the class of error this sheet opened with.
SWAP · A FITTED SHEET THAT REFUSES HONESTLY
Swap window
12 September – 12 October 2026
every 12 months
Koi can't perform the swap and doesn't pretend to.
Your records stay with the plan. The new car joins the same history; nothing is retyped.
Remind me on 12 September
The refusal is verbatim and it is stated without apology. Swap appends the new car to the plan's lineage: date-based reminders carry over, mileage-target reminders retire with the old car. The sheet says the first half in plain words; the reminder builder handles the second.
It is a fitted sheet, so the car page stays visible behind it and it closes itself — no Save button on something that only tells you a date.
PAYOFF NUDGE · A FINANCED CAR, ONCE EVER
PLAN
Bank · 289,00 € a month
48 payments, ending December 2026.
All 48 payments logged. Paid off?
Mark paid off Not yet
Not a modal, not a badge, not a red dot. A card on the car page, in the text voice, appearing one time when a finance plan passes its end date without a payoff.
Mark paid off flips ownership to owned, keeps every record, stops billing, and lands a milestone in History. Not yet is persisted and respected — the nudge never returns. The car form can flip it any time.
Neither fixture car can show this — the Golf is a subscription and the Ibiza is owned. Drawn on a hypothetical financed car and labelled as one, rather than bolted onto a car whose plan kind forbids it.

§6.5 · CAR FORM · FINANCED ROW UNFOLDED

The ownership rows unfold in place

Not a push, not a second sheet. And Switching keeps every record. Nothing to retype. sits directly under the radio group — where the fear actually is.

The odometer field is a baseline

Relabelled from "Odometer now" to Odometer at acquisition, with a sentence saying so. It is not a new reading — new readings are only ever minted by the odometer sheet, and a field that quietly mints one would break the fold rule from the very first screen.

Purchase price sits below the radios

Because it is a fact about the car, not about which ownership row is selected — Owned and Financed both show it. It is hidden entirely for subscriptions, which is inv. 15 enforced at the point of entry rather than filtered later.

Mark paid off is a real control here

Not just a sentence pointing at the car page's once-only nudge. Same consequence through either door — and the form's version is the one that still works after the user tapped Not yet.

Archive and Remove are different things

Archive → kept, restorable, out of tallies and reminders, hidden from the all-cars feed, one tap brings its records back, and a scoped view always shows them.
Remove → typed confirmation with the car's name, and there is no undo. Never conflated, never adjacent by accident.

Validation, at the door

Hard: empty make or model; year outside 1950…next; tank outside 10–200 L; power outside 20–2000 hp; odometer breaking monotonicity either direction — and that error names the conflicting record and offers to open it, which the build's message currently does not.

Fuel type is an enum, entered by chip. The build writes it as free text, so the client half of "flag, never fix" is applied to readings and not to cars.
